newsitem.title: USA: "Hollywood Madam" Fleiss pleads guilty in bargain.
newsitem.headline: "Hollywood Madam" Fleiss pleads guilty in bargain.

text.p: Reputed "Hollywood Madam" Heidi Fleiss, who provided prostitutes to the rich and famous, pleaded guilty in a plea bargain on Monday to one count of attempted pandering and was sentenced to 18 months in prison.

In return for the guilty plea, the state dropped all other pandering charges against her and Judge Judith Champagne ordered that her prison term run concurrently with her 37-month federal sentence for tax evasion.

"She's going to pay her debt to society and go on with her life," her lawyer Anthony Brooklier told reporters outside the court. He said he was still trying to get federal authorities to allow Fleiss to serve some of her time at a "boot camp" in Texas and hoped she could be at a half-way house by the end of the year.

Fleiss, 31, who ran a call-girl ring catering to the Hollywood power elite, was sentenced last month in federal court to 37 months for the tax evasion and money-laundering associated with the prostitution racket.

In 1995 she had been found guilty in state court of pandering -- procuring women for prostitution -- but that conviction was overturned for jury misconduct and a retrial was ordered. Since her federal conviction, her lawyers had been negotiating with prosecutors to drop the state retrial.

Deputy District Attorney Alan Carter told reporters the state was happy with the agreement. "We didn't see any interest in spending taxpayers' money to re-try the case," he said. "Were we out for blood? No."

Wearing khaki prison clothes and handcuffed in court, Fleiss barely audibly pleaded guilty to the single charge of attempted pandering. As she was escorted out of court after sentencing, she smiled weakly and shrugged her shoulders to reporters without saying a word.
Fleiss' attorney Brooklier commented: "She's a nice person and we're glad this is over for her."

During her first state trial, the jury heard that Fleiss supplied women to the rich and famous in Hollywood. Although the names in her "black book" were never revealed, actor Charlie Sheen acknowledged in videotaped testimony to paying her thousands of dollars for the services of prostitutes.
